paper_title: When Should Models Change Their Minds? Contextual Belief Management in Large Language Models
datasets_benchmarks: BeliefTrack, a novel closed-world benchmark introduced by the authors spanning two symbolic environments -- Rule Discovery (RD) and Circuit Diagnosis (CD) -- each with a finite belief space and symbolic verifiers enabling exact turn-level comparison between a model's predicted belief state and an oracle belief state. The benchmark includes three diagnostic trajectory splits: Dstay (tests whether belief is preserved when evidence is unchanged), Dupdate (tests whether belief is correctly revised after delayed correction), and Diso (tests isolation of task-irrelevant noise, evaluated under None/Sycophancy/Authority/Stress noise conditions). Standard capability benchmarks MMLU and GSM8K are used as general-ability controls to confirm RL training does not degrade base capabilities. Train/test splits are constructed at the oracle level (disjoint rule sets for RD, disjoint fault sets for CD) to prevent memorization and test generalization to unseen evidence-conditioned belief states.
models_evaluated: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3.5-9B are the two primary models used for the RL and BT-Prompt experiments (Table 1). Additionally, a pilot study evaluates three frontier models -- Qwen3.5-Plus, DeepSeek-V3.2, and GPT-5.2 -- on 135 Rule Discovery examples with task-irrelevant noise, all showing substantial belief-management error rates (46.7%, 31.9%, and 20.0% respectively, per Figure 1).
key_result: Vanilla models show severe Contextual Belief Management (CBM) failures: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct fails on 97-99% of trajectories across all three diagnostic metrics (Failed Stay Rate/FSR, Failed Update Rate/FUR, Failed Isolation Rate/FIR) in both RD and CD; Qwen3.5-9B is stronger but still fails substantially, with FIR reaching 95.4% in Circuit Diagnosis. paper_title: Mitigating Scaffolding Collapse in Socratic Tutors via Representation Alignment
datasets_benchmarks: A custom dataset built from TutorChat plus additional sourced problems, spanning five STEM tutoring domains (Math, Computer Science, Physics, Chemistry, Biology; 100 test samples per domain), comprising 500 positive (scaffold-preserving) trajectories and corresponding collapse-typed negative trajectories synthesized via Qwen3.6-27B rewriting. datasets_benchmarks: Two knowledge-based visual question answering datasets about named entities, converted from free-form to multiple-choice format: ViQuAE (3,697 original questions, 3,010 after MCQA construction, built on TriviaQA with named entities replaced by images) and InfoSeek (1.3M original questions across 11K+ visual entities from Wikidata templates, down-sampled to 3,000 MCQA samples to match ViQuAE's size). Acc) on the subset where the LVLM correctly identifies the depicted entity, Flip Rate (FR, rate of disagreement between the visual-modality answer and textual-modality answer for the same entity), and a derived lower-bound Conflict Rate (CR = FR - delta-Acc) that isolates true parametric knowledge conflict from mere performance-gap effects.
models_evaluated: Five open-source Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) spanning multiple architectures and scales: LLaVA-7b, LLaVA-13b, LLaVA-34b, InstructBlip-7b, and Qwen2-VL-7b. paper_title: A pen mark is all you need - Incidental prompt injection attacks on Vision Language Models in real-life histopathology
datasets_benchmarks: Author-constructed scenario suite over public whole-slide images: TCGA COAD-READ, THCA, OV and PRAD cohorts plus the TCIA SLN-Breast collection. N = 3888 total observations across three label categories, four clinically relevant tasks and 72 slides; sub-experiments include n = 1134 observations for the pen-label tasks, n = 810 for the watermark experiment over 30 WSIs (15 prostate, 15 ovarian), and n = 1944 unique observations each for native versus 'attention on tissue' prompting.
models_evaluated: Claude 3 Opus; Claude 3.5 Sonnet; GPT-4o
key_result: All three VLMs treated handwritten labels and watermarks as infallible ground truth: 90-100% accuracy when the label leaked the correct answer and 0-10% when the watermark was misleading, against clean baseline accuracies of only 30-65% on the same multiclass tasks. paper_title: Graph-Based Prompt Injection Attacks Against Large Language Models
datasets_benchmarks: 30 illegal prompts generated per model, each tested with 4 injection types x 30 trials against GPT-4/GPT-4o; no external benchmark, self-constructed attack set
models_evaluated: GPT-4; GPT-4o
key_result: The proposed graph-based injection (hiding sensitive words as math expressions rendered as a graph image) achieves up to 97% attack success rate (ASR) against GPT-4/GPT-4o, higher than ArtPrompt (~90%) and far higher than plain textual/visual prompt injection (0% ASR, fully blocked).

paper_title: Discerning and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts through Adaptive Decoding with Contextual Information-Entropy Constraint
datasets_benchmarks: NaturalQuestions; SQuAD 1.1; StrategyQA (each split post-hoc into conflicting vs non-conflicting subsets rather than synthetically perturbed); Counterfacts (Longpre et al. 2021, fully synthetic conflicts)
models_evaluated: LLaMA2-7B; LLaMA2-13B; OPT-6.7B; OPT-13B; FLAN-T5-3B; FLAN-T5-11B; GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (appendix comparison only)
key_result: COIECD improves over regular decoding on every realistic dataset while prior conflict-resolution decoders degrade on non-conflicting data: on NQ it gains EM +0.94/F1 +1.38 (LLaMA2-13B), +10.33 EM/+14.52 F1 (OPT-6.7B) and +2.84 EM/+1.67 F1 (FLAN-T5-3B), where contrastive decoding and context-aware decoding lose 8.38 and 7.09 EM respectively on FLAN-T5-3B.
